sources.title: Tanzil Quran Text (Uthmani, Version 1.1)
sources.author: Tanzil Project
sources.version: Version 1.1 (released February 2021); file downloaded 2026-10-22, copyright block dated 2007-2026
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0, with Tanzil's terms of use: verbatim copies only (changing the text is not allowed), the source (Tanzil Project) must be clearly indicated with a link to tanzil.net, and the copyright notice must be kept.
sources.credit: Quran text: Tanzil Project, Tanzil Quran Text (Uthmani, Version 1.1), CC BY 3.0, used verbatim. Check for updates at https://tanzil.net/
sources.notes: Downloaded from https://tanzil.net/pub/download/index.php with quranType=uthmani, outType=txt-2 (Text with aya numbers, 'sura|aya|text') and Tanzil's default options: pause marks on, sajdah signs on, rub-el-hizb signs off, tatweel below superscript alefs on, sequential tanweens off; agree=true. The raw file is kept verbatim in data/tanzil/quran-uthmani.txt and pinned by sha256 in scripts/fetch-quran.ts. data/quran.json stores each cited ayah as the NFC form of its line: for 34 of the 36 cited ayat NFC reorders combining marks (for example shadda after the vowel sign) or composes alef + madda into one code point. The result is canonically equivalent to the Tanzil line (same text under Unicode), not byte-identical. The Tanzil copyright block is kept verbatim in data/quran.json (meta.tanzilCopyright) and in LICENSES.

sources.notes: Interim choice, pending the owner's decision (see REVIEW.md). Kept because it is the only pinned, verifiable transliteration available to freeze: the Quran Foundation API may not be cached or bundled, and generating a transliteration from the Arabic would be machine-made scripture text that nobody has checked. Changes made by this project (CC BY 4.0): observed near the ring-plane crossing, so the thin equatorial band the rings hide and the polar caps are filled from the adjacent observed latitudes; moons and moon shadows that crossed the planet are replaced by their row's running median; resampled from 1800 x 900 to 1024 and 2048 wide and mip-mapped; encoded as KTX2 (ETC1S and UASTC, lossy). OPAL acknowledgement: "This work used data acquired from the NASA/ESA HST Space Telescope, associated with OPAL program (PI: Simon, GO13937), and archived by the Space Telescope Science Institute, which is operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy, Inc., under NASA contract NAS 5-26555. All maps are available at http://dx.doi.org/10.17909/T9G593." HLSP page: https://archive.stsci.edu/hlsp/opal (doi:10.17909/T9G593).

sources.title: A Full Sweep of Saturn's Rings (PIA11142), Cassini narrow-angle camera natural-colour mosaic, 2008-11-26
sources.author: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute
sources.version: PIA11142.tif, 12126 x 1439, about 7 km per pixel radially, retrieved 2026-10-23
sources.license: Public domain (NASA/JPL Photojournal; NASA's media usage guidelines apply: credit NASA, imply no endorsement).
sources.credit: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute
sources.notes: The colour of Saturn's rings in exploration (the RGB channels of public/assets/planets/saturn/rings-8192-rgba8.ktx2): the lit face seen from 10 degrees below it at 28 degrees phase, averaged across the arcs near the mosaic's apex and placed on ring radius by matching its gaps to the Cassini RSS optical-depth profile. Where the rings are thin the mosaic's brightness is divided by the share of a thick ring's light they return in its geometry (single scattering), so the strip holds the ring material's own colour; gaps and empty space take the nearest ring material's colour (straight alpha).

sources.title: Pioneer Venus Special Events Data bundle: the probes' atmosphere structure (LAS, SAS) and the Large Probe's nephelometer

sources.notes: Venus's descent (public/assets/descent/venus.json, scripts/descent/profiles.py): the Large Probe's pressure, temperature and density from 64.8 km above the 6,052.0 km radius to the ground (9 December 1978, 4.4 N, 304.0 E), the Day Probe's entry profile above 70.5 km, and the Large Probe's nephelometer backscatter placed at the altitudes its own clock gives.
